guideTitle: The Best Ultrawide Monitor Stands: Risers and Arms Compared
metaTitle: Best Ultrawide Monitor Stands: Risers and VESA Arms (2026)
metaDescription: We compared ultrawide monitor risers and VESA arms on platform size, weight capacity, adjustment, mounting method and extras, including options for 49-inch screens.
introParagraphs: "Ultrawide monitor stand" covers two different products. A riser is a platform that your monitor's own stand sits on: no VESA mount needed, usually cheaper, and often with storage underneath. An arm holds the monitor by its VESA pattern and adds height, tilt and rotation adjustment, but only works if the monitor has a VESA mount and its weight is within the arm's rating.

For ultrawides, weight and width are the constraints. A riser has to be wide and deep enough for the monitor's stand; an arm has to be rated for the panel's weight without its stand, and heavy 49-inch screens need a heavy-duty arm. Check your monitor's specifications before comparing anything else.

Our comparison is based on published specifications, including capacity, size support, adjustment and mounting method, plus price position, not hands-on testing. Prices range from about $27 to $94 at the time of writing.

westree-dual-monitor-stand-riser.summary: A 35.8-inch steel-and-wood riser rated for 150 lb, with storage underneath.
westree-dual-monitor-stand-riser.description:
The WESTREE is the riser to choose for a heavy ultrawide: a 35.8 x 10.2-inch steel-and-wood platform rated for 150 lb, the highest capacity here, with room underneath for a keyboard.

No VESA mount is needed, and WESTREE says it assembles in about two minutes. A non-slip surface keeps the monitor's stand in place.

Height is fixed, and there is no tilt or rotation. Check that your monitor's stand fits within the 10.2-inch depth.
westree-dual-monitor-stand-riser.bestFor: Heavy ultrawides, including large ones, where a simple lift is enough.
westree-dual-monitor-stand-riser.skipIf: You want to adjust height or tilt; an arm like the HUANUO TitanLift does that.

across-star-dual-monitor-stand-riser.summary: A modular riser that adjusts from 32 to 40 inches wide, rated for 80 lb.
across-star-dual-monitor-stand-riser.description:
The Across-Star is the lowest-priced option here and the only riser with adjustable length: its modular three-piece platform extends from 32 to 40 inches, so it can be sized to your desk and monitor.

It is metal and wood, rated for 80 lb, with storage space underneath, and needs no VESA mount.

The 80 lb rating is lower than the WESTREE's, though well above most single monitors, and height is fixed.
across-star-dual-monitor-stand-riser.bestFor: Desks where a riser needs to fit a specific width.
across-star-dual-monitor-stand-riser.skipIf: You need more capacity; the WESTREE is rated for 150 lb.

vivo-single-monitor-desk-stand-freestand.summary: A VESA stand with its own base, for monitors up to 38 inches, where clamping is not allowed.
vivo-single-monitor-desk-stand-freestand.description:
The VIVO freestanding stand is for desks you cannot clamp to, such as rentals, glass tops or shared offices: it holds the monitor by its VESA mount on a weighted steel base.

VIVO lists support for ultrawides up to 38 inches with VESA 75 or 100mm, 18 inches of lift, 360-degree rotation and 15 degrees of tilt either way.

The base takes desk space, and the listing does not state a weight limit, so check your monitor's weight against VIVO's full specifications.
vivo-single-monitor-desk-stand-freestand.bestFor: Desks where clamping is not possible or allowed.
vivo-single-monitor-desk-stand-freestand.skipIf: You can clamp to the desk and want more height; the VIVO extra-tall mount has a 39-inch pole.

vivo-extra-tall-single-monitor-desk-moun.summary: A 39-inch pole mount for ultrawides up to 38 inches and 22 lb, with wide tilt.
vivo-extra-tall-single-monitor-desk-moun.description:
The VIVO extra-tall mount is the pick for standing desks or tall users: its 39-inch pole is the tallest here, leaving room to position the screen high.

It supports ultrawides up to 38 inches and 22 lb, tilts 90 degrees either way and rotates 360 degrees, and mounts with a C-clamp or through a grommet. It is the most widely reviewed stand here.

The 22 lb limit rules out many heavier curved ultrawides, so check your panel's weight without its stand.
vivo-extra-tall-single-monitor-desk-moun.bestFor: Sit-stand desks and tall users with a lighter ultrawide.
vivo-extra-tall-single-monitor-desk-moun.skipIf: Your monitor weighs over 22 lb; the HUANUO TitanLift is rated for 44 lb.

vivo-dual-vertically-stacked-monitor-sta.summary: Stacks two ultrawides up to 34 inches vertically, 22 lb each.
vivo-dual-vertically-stacked-monitor-sta.description:
The VIVO stacked stand is for a specific layout: two ultrawides, up to 34 inches each, one above the other, which saves desk width compared with two screens side by side.

Each arm is rated for 22 lb on a 28.5-inch pole and tilts and rotates independently. It is steel and aluminum and mounts with a C-clamp or grommet.

It does not suit 49-inch screens, and the 22 lb per-arm limit rules out heavier panels.
vivo-dual-vertically-stacked-monitor-sta.skipIf: You use a single ultrawide; a single mount or riser is simpler.

oimaster-monitor-stand-riser-usb-hub.summary: A riser with three height settings, a USB 3.0 hub, USB-C port, drawer and phone holder.
oimaster-monitor-stand-riser-usb-hub.description:
The OImaster is the riser to choose if you want more than a shelf: it has three height settings (16.5, 18.5 and 20.5 inches as listed), a built-in USB 3.0 hub and USB-C port, a storage drawer and a phone holder.

It is ABS and metal, rated for 50 to 55 lb, and folds flat for storage.

It has fewer buyer reviews than the other risers, its capacity is lower, and height adjusts only in fixed steps. Check whether its platform width suits a wide monitor stand.
oimaster-monitor-stand-riser-usb-hub.bestFor: Buyers who want a riser that adds USB ports and small-item storage.
oimaster-monitor-stand-riser-usb-hub.skipIf: You have a very wide or heavy monitor stand; the WESTREE is larger and rated higher.

huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-monitor-arm-.summary: A heavy-duty arm for screens up to 49 inches and 44 lb, with a five-year warranty.
huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-monitor-arm-.description:
The HUANUO TitanLift is the only arm here rated for 49-inch super-ultrawides: HUANUO lists screens up to 49 inches and 44 lb, with an arm it says is 20 percent thicker and a base 30 percent wider than its standard model.

HUANUO states it has been tested through 50,000 movement cycles and backs it with a five-year warranty, the longest here. It uses a dual C-clamp.

It is the most expensive option here at the time of writing, needs a VESA-compatible monitor and a desk edge the clamp can grip.
cons: Needs VESA and a suitable desk edge
huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-monitor-arm-.bestFor: Owners of large or heavy ultrawides who want full arm adjustment.
huanuo-titanlift-heavy-duty-monitor-arm-.skipIf: You only need a lift; the WESTREE riser holds more weight for less.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A riser needs no VESA mount and adds storage; an arm adds adjustment and frees desk space but needs VESA and a suitable desk edge.
For arms, compare the panel's weight without its stand to the arm's rating. Here, VIVO arms are rated for 22 lb and the HUANUO for 44 lb.
VIVO lists support up to 38 inches (34 inches for the stacked stand); only the HUANUO arm is rated for 49 inches.
Check that the monitor's stand fits the platform's width and depth. The Across-Star adjusts from 32 to 40 inches wide.
C-clamps need a solid desk edge; grommet mounts need a hole; the VIVO freestanding stand needs neither.

faq.q: What's the difference between a monitor riser and a monitor arm?
faq.a: A riser is a platform the monitor's own stand sits on; it needs no VESA mount and often adds storage. An arm holds the monitor by its VESA mount and adds height, tilt and rotation adjustment.

faq.q: Do I need a VESA mount?
faq.a: Only for an arm or VESA stand. The WESTREE, Across-Star and OImaster risers do not need one. The VIVO and HUANUO stands need a compatible VESA pattern, typically 75 or 100mm.

faq.q: Which stand here works for a 49-inch super-ultrawide?
faq.a: The HUANUO TitanLift is the only arm here rated for 49-inch screens, up to 44 lb. The WESTREE riser's 150 lb rating also covers a 49-inch monitor's weight, as long as the monitor's own stand fits its platform.

faq.q: Can I start with a riser and move to an arm later?
faq.a: Yes, they are separate purchases. If you think you will want adjustment, check now that your monitor has a VESA mount and note its weight without the stand.

faq.q: Why choose a freestanding stand over a clamp arm?
faq.a: It avoids clamping, which helps in rentals, on glass desks or where clamps are not allowed. The trade-off is that its base takes desk space.

bottomLine: If you just want the screen higher, a riser is the simple and inexpensive route. The WESTREE handles the most weight, the Across-Star adjusts to your desk width for the lowest price, and the OImaster adds USB ports and height steps.

If you want adjustment, choose an arm rated for your panel. The VIVO extra-tall and freestanding stands suit lighter ultrawides up to 38 inches, the stacked VIVO suits two 34-inch screens, and the HUANUO TitanLift is worth paying more for with a heavy or 49-inch monitor.
